newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-LENS STRUGGLE WITH ON AND OFF-FIELD PROBLEMS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LENS STRUGGLE WITH ON AND OFF-FIELD PROBLEMS.

text.p: Fans of French first division club Lens have had a roller coaster ride this season.
Lens, whose support in France is second only to Marseille's in terms of passion, ruled the roost early in the season with four wins in four games, the only side with maximum points.
But since then they have won just four of their subsequent 22 matches -- three in a row in a mini-revival in October -- sinking to 16th, one place above the relegation zone.

Their dreams of a second successive season in Europe long dead, Lens, who have finished in the top 10 every season since promotion in 1991, will regard a point from their visit to Lyon on Friday as priceless.
Current leaders Monaco became the bane of their lives, ending their unbeaten run with a 5-1 rout in September, the prelude to first round UEFA Cup elimination by Lazio of Italy.
Monaco also won at Lens in the league in December, then put them out of the League Cup last month. They are also out of the French Cup.
Beleaguered coach Slavo Muslin said: "We no longer have the choice, we have to seize every point. The problem is simple, every time we think we've found the way to a cure, we fall again."
Muslin has seldom had a full squad from which to pick his team and against Lyon he will be without five first choice players.

Defender Frederic Dehu is suspended, Cyrille Magnier and Eric Sikora are still recovering from injury, Benin's Jean-Marc Adjovi-Boko and Marc-Vivien Foe of Cameroon will be away on African Nations' Cup duty and strikers Tony Vairelles and Sebastien Dallet are doubtful.
In December, the club suspended their young Russian Sacha Rychkov after he tested positive for cannabis, while playmaker Frederic Meyrieu was axed from the squad for below-par performances.

Lens, who have tested the patience of their fervent fans to the limit, are also expecting their Bollaert stadium to be banned for at least one game after a linesman was knocked out when he was struck by a bottle of water during last weekend's home defeat by Paris St Germain.
The fan responsible was jailed for a month and suspended from all football grounds for a year. The league's disciplinary commission is expected to rule on the incident next week.

Lens are also behind on alterations to their stadium for the 1998 World Cup finals. The work should be completed before June when they are due to host a match in the Tournoi de France warm-up tournament.
Two people involved in the work on the stadium were arrested last month and placed under investigation for fraud in public office.
